changes: added Flint 40B-A2.5B (Recursive; MoE, 39.8B total, about 2.5B active per the model card; Apache-2.0; 262k context; coding-agent model; GGUF from unsloth)
added Nanbeige4.3 33B (dense 33.1B; Apache-2.0; 512k context; GGUF from bartowski)
hardware: added NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X 128GB (6144-core Blackwell GPU, 128 GB LPDDR5X unified memory, 256-bit, 300 GB/s per NVIDIA's spec page and porting guide)
weekly measured-data refresh: LocalScore re-pulled, llama.cpp ROCm/Vulkan scoreboards and active performance threads re-fetched (336 measured points, was 332)
Added Qwen3.8 27B (dense, vision, Apache-2.0; 262k native context, up to 1M with YaRN per its model card). Widely used since August and was missing from the catalog.
Added LFM2.5 24B-A2B (Liquid AI MoE, 24B total / 2.45B active, LFM Open License v1.0, released Oct 13; official LiquidAI GGUF, Q4_K_M 14.5 GB).

Added Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B (NVIDIA hybrid Mamba-2/Transformer MoE with vision, OpenMDW-1.1, released Oct 15; Q4_K_M GGUF about 70 GB, so it needs a 96 GB GPU or a 128 GB+ unified-memory machine). llama.cpp support merged Oct 15 (ggml-org/llama.cpp PR #30520).
New hardware: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 (Ryzen AI Halo, announced Oct 12): 192 GB LPDDR5x-8533 on a 256-bit bus = 273 GB/s (computed from AMD's spec page), with its own hardware page.
KV-cache math now also covers Mamba-2 hybrid layers (Nemotron) and LFM2 short-convolution layers: only the attention layers grow with context; the other layers keep a small fixed-size state.

Benchmarks refreshed: 12 new rows from the llama.cpp CUDA thread (discussion #15013) and 5 new LocalScore rows. The M5 Max (40-core GPU) speed calibration moved from 0.78 to 0.61 with more data (n=11).
llama.cpp 0.7.0 (Oct 15) changed llama-server's default port from 8080 to 9931. Our commands do not set a port, so look for the server on 9931 unless you pass --port.
Context choices now go up to 1M tokens (256k, 512k, 1M added) plus a q4_0 KV cache option.

Contexts beyond a model's native maximum are shown only for models whose own card documents YaRN extension (Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Qwen3-Coder, Qwen3-VL) and are flagged "extended". All other models are excluded and listed with their real maximum.
KV cache now includes the fixed-size linear-attention state for Qwen3.5/3.6 hybrid models.
Speed at long context is an estimate with a depth penalty fitted to measured depth runs (tools/calibrate_depth.py); time-to-first-token is estimated from measured prompt-processing speed.
